h: Hackworth, Sans Pareil and the railway town
p: Shildon's railway story is closely tied to Timothy Hackworth, the engineer who ran the locomotive works for the Stockton and Darlington Railway. His locomotive Sans Pareil competed at the famous Rainhill Trials in 1829, the contest won by Stephenson's Rocket, and Sans Pareil is on display at Locomotion. It is a thrill to stand next to an engine from those very early days.

The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in 1825, and its bicentenary in 2025 brought a huge spotlight onto Shildon and the surrounding towns. Locomotion makes a great starting point if you want to understand why this corner of County Durham matters so much to the history of the railways.

Entry to the main museum is free, which makes it a brilliant low-cost day out for families. Some special events or rides may carry a charge, so check before you go if you have your eye on something particular.

Allow two to three hours to explore the collection building and the heritage buildings near the museum entrance, including Hackworth's former home. Little ones can run around outside while bigger train fans pore over the details.

For more railway history, head to Darlington, where the Head of Steam museum is based at the historic North Road station on the original railway route. Bishop Auckland, just up the road, has Auckland Castle and a bundle of galleries, and Durham's cathedral and castle are within easy reach for a proper heritage weekend.
